proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan mixing_order_reasoning: Stream A (acid + DPDTC + DMAP) must react fully in Stage 1 before benzylamine (Stream B) is introduced. A T-mixer (P-632 ETFE or P-713 PEEK, both available) joins Stage 1 effluent with Stream B between the two reactors. Premature contact of benzylamine with DPDTC would cause direct thiocarbonate amination instead of the desired sequential thioester-then-aminolysis pathway. The batch protocol explicitly adds benzylamine only after Stage 1 is complete, which this interstage T-mixer replicates in flow.

Prepare Stream B containing Benzylamine (1.05 equiv relative to substrate), 2-MeTHF (solvent) in 2-Methyltetrahydrofuran (2-MeTHF) at 2.1 M; concentration basis: chemistry_plan.
Install Stage 1 reactor coil_row12 (10 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 95 deg C.
Install Stage 2 reactor coil_row11 (5 mL, 2.4 mm ID, ETFE) at 95 deg C.
Install assigned feeds A:pump_e_series_blue, B:pump_e_series_blue.
Set the outlet BPR to 7 bar gauge and start liquid feeds at final outlet flow 0.2 mL/min.

Allow at least 2 reactor volumes (~30 mL total tubing + dead volume) to reach steady state before collecting product fractions for analysis.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
Collect only after the canonical residence-time stabilization period; use the inventory-compiled downstream path.
For shutdown, stop reactive cofeeds and reagent gas first, flush with a compatible declared solvent, then depressurize through the controlled outlet.

proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan mixing_order_reasoning: Stream A (acid + DPDTC + DMAP) must react fully in Stage 1 before benzylamine (Stream B) is introduced. A T-mixer (P-632 ETFE or P-713 PEEK, both available) joins Stage 1 effluent with Stream B between the two reactors. Premature contact of benzylamine with DPDTC would cause direct thiocarbonate amination instead of the desired sequential thioester-then-aminolysis pathway. The batch protocol explicitly adds benzylamine only after Stage 1 is complete, which this interstage T-mixer replicates in flow.

proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Chemistry Plan mixing_order_reasoning: Stream A (acid + DPDTC + DMAP) must react fully in Stage 1 before benzylamine (Stream B) is introduced. A T-mixer (P-632 ETFE or P-713 PEEK, both available) joins Stage 1 effluent with Stream B between the two reactors. Premature contact of benzylamine with DPDTC would cause direct thiocarbonate amination instead of the desired sequential thioester-then-aminolysis pathway. The batch protocol explicitly adds benzylamine only after Stage 1 is complete, which this interstage T-mixer replicates in flow.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

uncertainties: specific uncertainty

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

DrChemistry.justification: Highest limiting feed throughput (0.14 mmol/min) with compact 5+5 mL ETFE geometry. Stage 1 τ=17.9 min (ratio 0.60), Stage 2 τ=14.3 min (ratio 0.48); both sub-batch, suitable as a compact starting screen. Single reactor type simplifies setup. Stream B flow 0.07 mL/min is comfortably above peristaltic minimum.
uncertainties: Sub-batch Stage 1 exposure may be insufficient for complete thioester formation — experimentally uncharacterized.
Sub-batch Stage 2 aminolysis exposure adequacy is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Mixed reactor geometry (2 mL PFA Stage 1, 5 mL ETFE Stage 2). Stage 1 τ=16.7 min (ratio 0.56) sub-batch; Stage 2 τ=33.3 min (ratio 1.11) exceeds batch anchor. Throughput 0.06 mmol/min, lower than C1. Stream B at 0.03 mL/min approaches low-flow pulsation risk.
uncertainties: Stream B at 0.03 mL/min may exhibit peristaltic pulsation; mixing quality uncertain.
Whether Stage 2 over-exposure at 95 °C benefits or degrades amide yield is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=35.7 min (ratio 1.19) exceeds batch anchor; Stage 2 τ=14.3 min (ratio 0.48) sub-batch. Throughput matches C1 at 0.14 mmol/min. Uses 10+5 mL ETFE. Tests whether extended thioester activation improves amide stage performance, with compact Stage 2.
uncertainties: Whether prolonged Stage 1 at 95 °C degrades thioester intermediate is uncharacterized.
Sub-batch Stage 2 aminolysis adequacy is uncharacterized.

DrChemistry.justification: Both stages near-batch (τ1=31.3 min ratio 1.04, τ2=25 min ratio 0.83) using 5+5 mL ETFE. Throughput 0.08 mmol/min. Compact interpretable baseline close to batch anchors for both stages.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 25 min is 17% below batch anchor; adequacy for aminolysis is uncharacterized.
Near-batch times are not guaranteed optimal in flow.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=25 min (ratio 0.83) sub-batch; Stage 2 τ=50 min (ratio 1.67) well above batch. Mixed 2+5 mL geometry. Throughput 0.04 mmol/min (lowest tier). Stream B at 0.02 mL/min is at E-series peristaltic minimum, raising pulsation risk.
uncertainties: Stream B at 0.02 mL/min is at minimum flow; pulsation and stoichiometric accuracy are at risk.
Stage 2 over-exposure effect on amide stability is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=62.5 min (ratio 2.08) strongly exceeds batch; Stage 2 τ=25 min (ratio 0.83) sub-batch. 10+5 mL ETFE. Throughput 0.08 mmol/min. Tests whether very long thioester activation is needed, with shorter aminolysis.
uncertainties: Thioester stability under 62.5 min at 95 °C is uncharacterized; degradation risk is a hypothesis.
Stage 2 aminolysis adequacy at 25 min sub-batch is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Both stages well above batch (τ1=62.5, τ2=50 min). Uses two 10 mL ETFE coils (coil_row12 qty=2, confirmed). Total time 112.5 min; throughput 0.08 mmol/min. Long-exposure anchor for screening; tests upper bound of exposure space.
uncertainties: Extended exposure of thioester intermediate at 95 °C may risk degradation — uncharacterized.
Long total processing time conflicts with throughput objective.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=16.7 min sub-batch; Stage 2 τ=66.7 min (ratio 2.22) well above batch. Mixed 2+10 mL. Throughput 0.06 mmol/min. Stream B at 0.03 mL/min near low-flow limit. Tests asymmetric short activation / long aminolysis.
uncertainties: Stream B at 0.03 mL/min pulsation risk for peristaltic pump.
Stage 2 amide product stability under 66.7 min at 95 °C is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=62.5 min (ratio 2.08); Stage 2 τ=20 min (ratio 0.67) sub-batch using compact 2 mL PFA. Throughput 0.04 mmol/min. Stream B at 0.02 mL/min is at E-series minimum. Tests long activation / short aminolysis geometry inversion.
uncertainties: Stream B at 0.02 mL/min is at minimum; stoichiometric and mixing fidelity uncertain.
Whether 20 min aminolysis is adequate is experimentally unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 2 τ=100 min (ratio 3.33) is the longest Stage 2 in the set; total time 125 min. Throughput 0.04 mmol/min (lowest tier). Stream B at 0.02 mL/min at minimum flow. Strongly imbalanced against balanced-priority objective; extreme over-exposure risk with minimum throughput.
uncertainties: Amide product or intermediate degradation under 100 min at 95 °C is uncharacterized.
Stream B minimum flow pulsation risk.

DrChemistry.justification: Same τ profile as C9 (62.5+20 min) but Stage 1 uses PFA 5 mL (coil_row4, 1 mm ID) giving higher pressure drop; Stage 2 uses PFA 2 mL. Throughput 0.04 mmol/min; Stream B at 0.02 mL/min minimum. Redundant with C9 in exposure space but different reactor geometry.
uncertainties: Stream B at minimum flow introduces stoichiometric fidelity risk.
Narrower ID (1 mm) Stage 1 increases pressure drop; solids deposition risk if any precipitation occurs.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=62.5, Stage 2 τ=50 min using two 5 mL ETFE coils (same IDs as C7 but smaller reactors at same flow). Total time 112.5 min; throughput 0.04 mmol/min (lowest). Stream B at 0.02 mL/min minimum. Duplicates long-exposure space of C7 at lower throughput; poor balance for balanced-priority objective.

DrKinetics.justification: Highest feed throughput (0.14 mmol/min), shortest total time (32.1 min). Both stages sub-batch (S1: 17.9 min/0.60×; S2: 14.3 min/0.48×). Compact identical-coil setup. Good throughput anchor; yield risk unquantified at both shortened stages.
uncertainties: Stage 1 thioester formation may be incomplete at 17.9 min (0.60× batch); uncharacterized.

DrKinetics.justification: Lower feed throughput (0.06 mmol/min). Stage 1 sub-batch (16.7 min, 0.56×); Stage 2 above batch (33.3 min, 1.11×). Asymmetric hold explores whether extended aminolysis compensates for short thioester stage. Mixed reactor types (PFA 2 mL + ETFE 5 mL).
uncertainties: Stage 1 thioester completeness at 16.7 min uncharacterized.

DrKinetics.justification: Highest feed throughput (0.14 mmol/min) with Stage 1 above batch (35.7 min, 1.19×), giving thioester formation headroom. Stage 2 shortened (14.3 min, 0.48×). Practical starting point balancing throughput and Stage 1 yield adequacy; Stage 2 risk is the key experimental question.
uncertainties: Stage 2 aminolysis at 14.3 min (0.48× batch) may be incomplete; requires experimental confirmation.

DrKinetics.justification: Stage 1 near-batch (31.3 min, 1.04×); Stage 2 shortened but substantial (25 min, 0.83×). Moderate feed throughput (0.08 mmol/min). Best interpretable baseline: near-batch Stage 1 minimizes thioester risk while Stage 2 shortening is modest. Compact identical-coil design.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 25 min (0.83×) may not fully complete aminolysis; kinetics uncharacterized.

request.task: Audit cross-domain conflicts and unsupported scientific claims. Return extra vetoes only for identified hard violations.

calls.system: You are a FlowPilot council reviewer. Return JSON only with concise evidence-based justification, not hidden reasoning. Authority: measured evidence > hard constraints > protocol facts > hypotheses > inference. These are unvalidated experimental SCREENS, not proven processes. Do not invent conversion, yield, kinetics, or residence-time superiority. No global shortest-time objective, 30% conversion floor, or class intensification factor. Batch residence times are screening anchors, not guaranteed flow optima. Review the COMPLETE connected process. Apply the explicit objective_policy to preferences. Near-batch times are not inherently the best choice. For yield priority compare adequate exposure in ALL stages against longer-time degradation risks, especially at a lower temperature. For throughput priority distinguish feed throughput from unmeasured product throughput. For gas stages, gas_flow_sccm and Q_gas_sccm mean mL/min at inlet/STP (273.15 K, 1.01325 bar). Their apparent residence-time index is V/(Q_liquid+Q_gas_STP), not measured liquid residence or photon exposure. Gas equivalents are proposed delivered molar ratios, not established stoichiometric consumption or uptake. If source_context.gas_delivery.requires_chemist_confirmation is true, explicitly report the gas-source change as unapproved and requiring laboratory review before use. Irradiation sources and wavelengths must be stage-assigned; no optical intensification or light-dose adequacy is proven. Use computed_comparisons for quantitative statements: target multipliers are not actual achieved hold ratios. Do not call unequal achieved ratios symmetric or claim highest throughput without checking all candidates. Honor equipment_boundary and scope: a union is not a T-mixer; an untested cooling hypothesis does not remove a hard constraint. State reduced-temperature compensation and comparative degradation risk as untested hypotheses, never established facts. Account for temperature deviations, later feed dilution and addition order, equipment and unanswered safety/solubility issues. Do not rewrite candidate numbers. A hard violation vetoes a candidate; an unresolved experimental outcome is an uncertainty, not proof of failure. Keep each candidate justification under 45 words and each uncertainty under 20 words. Use a shared assessment for issues common to all candidates.

computed_comparisons.batch_total_excludes: Cooling, charging, workup and other handling time are excluded from the summed reaction holds.
computed_comparisons.scope: These twelve screens vary stage-time coordinates and compatible reactor geometry within the upstream topology. They do not compare cooled versus direct interstage transfer and do not optimize gas equivalents. A gas-stage inlet/STP time ratio is not a ratio of liquid exposure to batch exposure.
computed_comparisons.equipment_boundary: A two-port union is not a three-port T-mixer. An assumed_standard_accessory mixer is a separate unconfirmed item, not a confirmed union capability.
computed_comparisons.evidence_boundary: Computed feed throughput is not measured product throughput. No measured time-temperature compensation, yield or comparative degradation ranking is available.

DrChemistry.justification: Highest limiting feed throughput (0.14 mmol/min) with compact 5+5 mL ETFE geometry. Stage 1 τ=17.9 min (ratio 0.60), Stage 2 τ=14.3 min (ratio 0.48); both sub-batch, suitable as a compact starting screen. Single reactor type simplifies setup. Stream B flow 0.07 mL/min is comfortably above peristaltic minimum.
uncertainties: Sub-batch Stage 1 exposure may be insufficient for complete thioester formation — experimentally uncharacterized.
Sub-batch Stage 2 aminolysis exposure adequacy is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Mixed reactor geometry (2 mL PFA Stage 1, 5 mL ETFE Stage 2). Stage 1 τ=16.7 min (ratio 0.56) sub-batch; Stage 2 τ=33.3 min (ratio 1.11) exceeds batch anchor. Throughput 0.06 mmol/min, lower than C1. Stream B at 0.03 mL/min approaches low-flow pulsation risk.
uncertainties: Stream B at 0.03 mL/min may exhibit peristaltic pulsation; mixing quality uncertain.
Whether Stage 2 over-exposure at 95 °C benefits or degrades amide yield is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=35.7 min (ratio 1.19) exceeds batch anchor; Stage 2 τ=14.3 min (ratio 0.48) sub-batch. Throughput matches C1 at 0.14 mmol/min. Uses 10+5 mL ETFE. Tests whether extended thioester activation improves amide stage performance, with compact Stage 2.
uncertainties: Whether prolonged Stage 1 at 95 °C degrades thioester intermediate is uncharacterized.
Sub-batch Stage 2 aminolysis adequacy is uncharacterized.

DrChemistry.justification: Both stages near-batch (τ1=31.3 min ratio 1.04, τ2=25 min ratio 0.83) using 5+5 mL ETFE. Throughput 0.08 mmol/min. Compact interpretable baseline close to batch anchors for both stages.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 25 min is 17% below batch anchor; adequacy for aminolysis is uncharacterized.
Near-batch times are not guaranteed optimal in flow.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=25 min (ratio 0.83) sub-batch; Stage 2 τ=50 min (ratio 1.67) well above batch. Mixed 2+5 mL geometry. Throughput 0.04 mmol/min (lowest tier). Stream B at 0.02 mL/min is at E-series peristaltic minimum, raising pulsation risk.
uncertainties: Stream B at 0.02 mL/min is at minimum flow; pulsation and stoichiometric accuracy are at risk.
Stage 2 over-exposure effect on amide stability is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=62.5 min (ratio 2.08) strongly exceeds batch; Stage 2 τ=25 min (ratio 0.83) sub-batch. 10+5 mL ETFE. Throughput 0.08 mmol/min. Tests whether very long thioester activation is needed, with shorter aminolysis.
uncertainties: Thioester stability under 62.5 min at 95 °C is uncharacterized; degradation risk is a hypothesis.
Stage 2 aminolysis adequacy at 25 min sub-batch is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Both stages well above batch (τ1=62.5, τ2=50 min). Uses two 10 mL ETFE coils (coil_row12 qty=2, confirmed). Total time 112.5 min; throughput 0.08 mmol/min. Long-exposure anchor for screening; tests upper bound of exposure space.
uncertainties: Extended exposure of thioester intermediate at 95 °C may risk degradation — uncharacterized.
Long total processing time conflicts with throughput objective.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=16.7 min sub-batch; Stage 2 τ=66.7 min (ratio 2.22) well above batch. Mixed 2+10 mL. Throughput 0.06 mmol/min. Stream B at 0.03 mL/min near low-flow limit. Tests asymmetric short activation / long aminolysis.
uncertainties: Stream B at 0.03 mL/min pulsation risk for peristaltic pump.
Stage 2 amide product stability under 66.7 min at 95 °C is unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=62.5 min (ratio 2.08); Stage 2 τ=20 min (ratio 0.67) sub-batch using compact 2 mL PFA. Throughput 0.04 mmol/min. Stream B at 0.02 mL/min is at E-series minimum. Tests long activation / short aminolysis geometry inversion.
uncertainties: Stream B at 0.02 mL/min is at minimum; stoichiometric and mixing fidelity uncertain.
Whether 20 min aminolysis is adequate is experimentally unknown.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 2 τ=100 min (ratio 3.33) is the longest Stage 2 in the set; total time 125 min. Throughput 0.04 mmol/min (lowest tier). Stream B at 0.02 mL/min at minimum flow. Strongly imbalanced against balanced-priority objective; extreme over-exposure risk with minimum throughput.
uncertainties: Amide product or intermediate degradation under 100 min at 95 °C is uncharacterized.
Stream B minimum flow pulsation risk.

DrChemistry.justification: Same τ profile as C9 (62.5+20 min) but Stage 1 uses PFA 5 mL (coil_row4, 1 mm ID) giving higher pressure drop; Stage 2 uses PFA 2 mL. Throughput 0.04 mmol/min; Stream B at 0.02 mL/min minimum. Redundant with C9 in exposure space but different reactor geometry.
uncertainties: Stream B at minimum flow introduces stoichiometric fidelity risk.
Narrower ID (1 mm) Stage 1 increases pressure drop; solids deposition risk if any precipitation occurs.

DrChemistry.justification: Stage 1 τ=62.5, Stage 2 τ=50 min using two 5 mL ETFE coils (same IDs as C7 but smaller reactors at same flow). Total time 112.5 min; throughput 0.04 mmol/min (lowest). Stream B at 0.02 mL/min minimum. Duplicates long-exposure space of C7 at lower throughput; poor balance for balanced-priority objective.
uncertainties: Stream B minimum flow pulsation risk.
Extended Stage 2 amide stability at 95 °C is uncharacterized.

DrKinetics.justification: Highest feed throughput (0.14 mmol/min), shortest total time (32.1 min). Both stages sub-batch (S1: 17.9 min/0.60×; S2: 14.3 min/0.48×). Compact identical-coil setup. Good throughput anchor; yield risk unquantified at both shortened stages.
uncertainties: Stage 1 thioester formation may be incomplete at 17.9 min (0.60× batch); uncharacterized.
Stage 2 aminolysis at 14.3 min (0.48× batch) may give incomplete amide yield; uncharacterized.

DrKinetics.justification: Lower feed throughput (0.06 mmol/min). Stage 1 sub-batch (16.7 min, 0.56×); Stage 2 above batch (33.3 min, 1.11×). Asymmetric hold explores whether extended aminolysis compensates for short thioester stage. Mixed reactor types (PFA 2 mL + ETFE 5 mL).
uncertainties: Stage 1 thioester completeness at 16.7 min uncharacterized.
No evidence extended Stage 2 compensates for sub-batch Stage 1.

DrKinetics.justification: Highest feed throughput (0.14 mmol/min) with Stage 1 above batch (35.7 min, 1.19×), giving thioester formation headroom. Stage 2 shortened (14.3 min, 0.48×). Practical starting point balancing throughput and Stage 1 yield adequacy; Stage 2 risk is the key experimental question.
uncertainties: Stage 2 aminolysis at 14.3 min (0.48× batch) may be incomplete; requires experimental confirmation.
Thioester stability during extended Stage 1 hold is uncharacterized.

DrKinetics.justification: Stage 1 near-batch (31.3 min, 1.04×); Stage 2 shortened but substantial (25 min, 0.83×). Moderate feed throughput (0.08 mmol/min). Best interpretable baseline: near-batch Stage 1 minimizes thioester risk while Stage 2 shortening is modest. Compact identical-coil design.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 25 min (0.83×) may not fully complete aminolysis; kinetics uncharacterized.
Direct interstage transfer at 95°C without cooling requires chemist confirmation.

DrKinetics.justification: Lowest feed throughput tier (0.04 mmol/min). Stage 1 sub-batch (25 min, 0.83×); Stage 2 well above batch (50 min, 1.67×). Explores whether long aminolysis time recovers yield from shorter thioester stage. Limited throughput value for balanced objective.
uncertainties: Stage 1 thioester completeness at 25 min uncharacterized.
Stage 2 extended hold at 95°C: product stability over 50 min uncharacterized.

DrKinetics.justification: Stage 1 greatly extended (62.5 min, 2.08×); Stage 2 sub-batch (25 min, 0.83×). Moderate feed throughput (0.08 mmol/min). Long Stage 1 at 95°C raises thioester/intermediate stability concern. Provides screening data on over-extended Stage 1.
uncertainties: Thioester or intermediate stability at 62.5 min / 95°C is uncharacterized; degradation risk is a hypothesis.
Stage 2 at 25 min (0.83× batch) may be incomplete.

DrKinetics.justification: Both stages well above batch (S1: 62.5 min 2.08×; S2: 50 min 1.67×). Total 112.5 min. Uses two ETFE 10 mL coils. Lowest throughput-per-time ratio in the set. Useful only as an extended-hold upper bound; limited practical value for balanced objective.
uncertainties: Extended exposure at 95°C across both stages: intermediate and product stability uncharacterized.
No evidence prolonged hold improves yield beyond batch.

DrKinetics.justification: Stage 1 sub-batch (16.7 min, 0.56×); Stage 2 greatly extended (66.7 min, 2.22×). Moderate feed throughput (0.06 mmol/min). Explores maximum aminolysis time; however very long Stage 2 at 95°C with uncharacterized product stability is a concern.
uncertainties: Stage 1 thioester completeness at 16.7 min uncharacterized.
Product degradation at 66.7 min / 95°C is an untested hypothesis.

DrKinetics.justification: Stage 1 greatly extended (62.5 min, 2.08×) using ETFE 5 mL; Stage 2 compressed (20 min, 0.67×) in small PFA 2 mL coil. Lowest throughput tier (0.04 mmol/min). Mirrors C3 logic inverted but at lower throughput; Stage 2 shortening risk similar.
uncertainties: Stage 2 aminolysis at 20 min (0.67×) may be incomplete; uncharacterized.
Stage 1 intermediate stability at 62.5 min / 95°C uncharacterized.

DrKinetics.justification: Stage 2 at 100 min (3.33× batch) is the longest Stage 2 in the set. Lowest throughput (0.04 mmol/min), total 125 min. Extreme upper bound for aminolysis hold. Product stability over 100 min at 95°C is an unresolved safety/chemistry concern warranting careful review.
uncertainties: Product or byproduct accumulation at 100 min / 95°C: degradation risk uncharacterized.
Practical value for balanced objective is limited at 0.04 mmol/min throughput.

DrKinetics.justification: Stage 1 at 62.5 min (2.08×) in PFA 5 mL 1 mm ID; Stage 2 at 20 min (0.67×) in PFA 2 mL. Identical throughput to C9 (0.04 mmol/min) with different reactor geometry. Narrow-bore PFA in Stage 1 increases axial dispersion risk vs. ETFE 2.4 mm alternatives at same flow.
uncertainties: Stage 2 aminolysis at 20 min (0.67×) may be incomplete; uncharacterized.
Axial dispersion behavior in 1 mm ID vs. 2.4 mm ID coils at low Re not characterized.

DrKinetics.justification: Both stages substantially above batch (S1: 62.5 min; S2: 50 min) using two ETFE 5 mL coils. Lowest throughput tier (0.04 mmol/min). Symmetrically extended screen; duplicates C7 concept at lower total reactor volume. Limited additional information versus C7.
uncertainties: Extended dual-stage hold at 95°C: intermediate and product stability uncharacterized.
Screen informativeness overlap with C7 reduces marginal value.

DrFluidics.justification: Highest substrate feed throughput (0.14 mmol/min). Compact 5+5 mL ETFE geometry. Stage 1: 17.9 min (0.60× batch); Stage 2: 14.3 min (0.48× batch). Both stages below batch anchor — thioester completion and amide formation under shorter exposure are unvalidated but acceptable screening entry points per balanced objective. Single reactor type simplifies setup.
uncertainties: Both stages below batch anchor; thioester and amide completion at shorter exposure unconfirmed.
Direct interstage transfer at 95°C without cooling is an untested hypothesis.
T-mixer for Stage 2 Stream B injection not explicitly assigned.

DrFluidics.justification: Reduced throughput (0.06 mmol/min). Stage 1 at 16.7 min (0.56× batch) is sub-batch; Stage 2 at 33.3 min (1.11× batch) exceeds batch anchor for amide coupling. Mixed reactor geometry (PFA 2 mL + ETFE 5 mL). Useful for probing whether longer Stage 2 benefits amide yield versus Stage 1 risk.
uncertainties: Thioester completion adequacy at 16.7 min Stage 1 is unconfirmed.
Whether extended Stage 2 compensates for incomplete Stage 1 is unknown.

DrFluidics.justification: Highest substrate feed throughput (0.14 mmol/min), equal to C1. Stage 1 at 35.7 min (1.19× batch) exceeds batch anchor — more conservative thioester formation. Stage 2 at 14.3 min (0.48× batch) is shorter. Balanced design favoring Stage 1 completion. Requires two different ETFE coils (10+5 mL).
uncertainties: Stage 2 sub-batch exposure for amide coupling; aminolysis completion at 14.3 min unconfirmed.
coil_row12 (10 mL ETFE, qty 2) and coil_row11 (5 mL ETFE, qty 2) inventory must be confirmed as simultaneously available.

DrFluidics.justification: Throughput 0.08 mmol/min. Stage 1: 31.25 min (1.04× batch); Stage 2: 25 min (0.83× batch). Both stages near batch anchor — interpretable baseline. Uses two 5 mL ETFE coils. Adequate balance but lower throughput than C1/C3.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 25 min is slightly sub-batch; amide completion not established.
Identical reactor assignment (coil_row11 ×2) requires confirmation of dual availability.

DrFluidics.justification: Low throughput (0.04 mmol/min). Stage 1: 25 min (0.83× batch); Stage 2: 50 min (1.67× batch). Long Stage 2 at 95°C — whether extended amide exposure risks degradation is uncharacterized but a concern. Useful as yield-bias long-Stage-2 data point.
uncertainties: Extended Stage 2 at 95°C degradation risk is uncharacterized.
Stage 1 sub-batch exposure may yield incomplete thioester.

DrFluidics.justification: Throughput 0.08 mmol/min. Stage 1: 62.5 min (2.08× batch) — substantially extended thioester exposure. Stage 2: 25 min (0.83× batch). Useful for probing whether excess Stage 1 time causes DPDTC-side product buildup. Requires 10+5 mL ETFE.
uncertainties: Prolonged Stage 1 at 95°C may generate DPDTC-derived side products; no evidence either way.
Stage 2 sub-batch for aminolysis.

DrFluidics.justification: Throughput 0.08 mmol/min. Both stages substantially above batch anchor (2.08×, 1.67×). Total time 112.5 min. Longest-total-time candidate at this throughput. Useful as upper-bound exposure reference. Requires two 10 mL ETFE coils simultaneously.
uncertainties: Risk of prolonged 95°C exposure in both stages — degradation potential uncharacterized.
coil_row12 (qty 2) dual use must be confirmed.

DrFluidics.justification: Throughput 0.06 mmol/min. Stage 1: 16.7 min (0.56× batch); Stage 2: 66.7 min (2.22× batch) — extreme Stage 2 extension at 95°C. Tests whether very long amide exposure degrades product. Mixed PFA 2 mL + ETFE 10 mL geometry.
uncertainties: 66.7 min Stage 2 at 95°C — product degradation risk is uncharacterized but elevated.
Incomplete Stage 1 thioester combined with long Stage 2 complicates interpretation.

DrFluidics.justification: Throughput 0.04 mmol/min. Stage 1: 62.5 min in 5 mL ETFE; Stage 2: 20 min in 2 mL PFA. Long Stage 1, short Stage 2. Reactor size inversion (larger to smaller) is hydraulically valid. Useful probe of over-extended Stage 1 with compressed amide stage.
uncertainties: Stage 2 at 20 min (0.67× batch) — aminolysis adequacy unconfirmed.
Reactor geometry inversion (ETFE→PFA, 2.4→1.0 mm ID) introduces mixing regime change at Stage 2 entry.

DrFluidics.justification: Throughput 0.04 mmol/min. Stage 1: 25 min; Stage 2: 100 min (3.33× batch). Longest Stage 2 in set. Useful as extreme upper bound for amide coupling; however, prolonged 95°C exposure risk is uncharacterized. Total time 125 min.
uncertainties: 100 min Stage 2 at 95°C — product degradation risk is uncharacterized and a notable concern.
Lowest throughput limits utility as baseline.

DrFluidics.justification: Throughput 0.04 mmol/min. Stage 1: 62.5 min in PFA 5 mL (1 mm ID); Stage 2: 20 min in PFA 2 mL. Identical to C9 in residence times but uses PFA coil_row4 for Stage 1 instead of ETFE coil_row11. Narrower ID (1 mm vs 2.4 mm) yields higher Re and better radial mixing in Stage 1.
uncertainties: Mixing regime difference between Stage 1 (1 mm PFA) and Stage 2 (1 mm PFA) is modest but ID change at junction entry with Stream B needs mixer confirmation.
Same aminolysis adequacy concern as C9 at 20 min Stage 2.

DrFluidics.justification: Throughput 0.04 mmol/min. Stage 1: 62.5 min; Stage 2: 50 min; total 112.5 min. Both stages well above batch anchor. Lowest throughput with longest combined hold at 95°C. Useful only as extreme degradation-risk reference; not preferred for balanced objective.
uncertainties: Combined 112.5 min at 95°C — degradation risk across both stages is uncharacterized.
Two 5 mL ETFE coils (coil_row11, qty 2) simultaneously required — confirm dual availability.

DrSafety.justification: Highest substrate throughput (0.14 mmol/min). Compact dual ETFE 5 mL coil design. Stage 1 τ=17.9 min (ratio 0.60×batch), Stage 2 τ=14.3 min (0.48×batch)—both sub-batch, consistent with balanced screening intent. Single platform, no equipment conflicts.
uncertainties: Sub-batch holds for both stages: thioester completeness and amide yield at shorter exposures unvalidated.
Stream B at 2.1 M benzylamine in 2-MeTHF: solubility unconfirmed.
Direct hot interstage transfer without cooling: chemical acceptability unvalidated.
E-series peristaltic accuracy at 0.07 mL/min (Stream B) requires verification.

DrSafety.justification: Moderate throughput (0.06 mmol/min). Stage 1 τ=16.7 min (0.56×batch) in compact 2 mL PFA coil; Stage 2 τ=33.3 min (1.11×batch) in 5 mL ETFE coil—asymmetric design providing extended Stage 2 exposure. Mixed reactor geometry is operationally straightforward.
uncertainties: Stage 1 sub-batch: thioester conversion at 16.7 min unvalidated.

selection.objective_alignment: Balanced priority requires maximum feed throughput, stable operation, and adequate stage exposure. C3 meets throughput parity with C1 while reducing the Stage 1 thioester-completion risk that C1 accepts by holding both stages sub-batch. The trade-off is accepting a sub-batch Stage 2 (0.48×) in exchange for S1 adequacy at maximum throughput; this is chemically justified as a starting screen because aminolysis of activated thioesters is generally faster than thioester formation, but that hypothesis is uncharacterized and requires experimental confirmation. Total time 50 min versus C1's 32 min reflects the S1 extension, not an inherent optimum.

alternatives.reason_not_selected: C1 shares the highest feed throughput (0.14 mmol/min) and is the more aggressive compact screen (S1 τ=17.9 min, 0.60×; S2 τ=14.3 min, 0.48×). Both stages are sub-batch, leaving thioester formation adequacy uncharacterized at S1. C3 is preferred as the first screen because it retains throughput parity while reducing S1 risk. C1 is the recommended co-first screen if C3 shows adequate S2 yield, to test whether S1 can be further compressed.

C4 provides the most interpretable near-batch baseline (S1 τ=31.3 min, 1.04×; S2 τ=25 min, 0.83×) at 0.08 mmol/min, which is 43% lower feed throughput than C3. The balanced objective prefers the higher-throughput C3 as a starting screen; C4 is designated the baseline reference if C3 or C1 show yield deficiency attributable to sub-batch S2 exposure. Near-batch times are not inherently optimal in flow; C4 does not supersede C3 on yield grounds absent measured evidence.

council_answer_assessments.effect: C3's maximum-throughput, conservative-S1 design directly addresses the balance of yield adequacy and throughput; sub-batch S2 is the unresolved element that experimental data will resolve.

C3 operationalizes the chemist hypothesis that direct hot interstage transfer is acceptable and that S1 completeness is the governing constraint; both remain unvalidated. S1 extended beyond batch anchor partially hedges the thioester-formation risk.

No historical yield data are available; candidate ranking is based solely on throughput, stage exposure ratios, and equipment feasibility. Measured yield from C3 would become the primary evidence for subsequent stage-time decisions.
